title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Avicena, which links AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers, raised a $100M+ Series C led by Intervest, with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD (Cristian Dina/The Next Web)
items.content_text: Sunnyvale-based Avicena has raised over $100M in Series C funding, led by InterVest with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD. The company's LightBundle platform utilizes MicroLED arrays instead of traditional lasers to address bandwidth and power bottlenecks in data movement between processors and memory in AI clusters.

items.title: After OpenAI and Anthropic shut the door on their data, a Chinese AI developer is turning to Google and Meta instead
items.content_text: Chinese AI companies Z.AI and Moonshot AI have to delay their next flagship models and are looking for new sources of training data. The effects now reach beyond previously known delays, after the US closed the cloud loophole for Nvidia chips, Nvidia halted shipments to Southeast Asia, and US companies cracked down on model distillation. As a result, Z.AI's roughly 3-trillion-parameter GLM-5.5 model, planned for November, is likely to slip into the first quarter of 2027, Reuters reports, citing

items.title: Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
items.content_text: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has resumed environmental permitting for data centers under a directive from outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott. The approvals include SpaceX's $24 billion gas-fired power and supercomputing complex near Brownsville, as developers scramble to secure rights before incoming Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa takes office in January with a mandate to curtail industry expansion and tax incentives.

items.title: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers by 2040
items.content_text: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites as part of the 'Starmind' constellation. This initiative aims to establish orbital compute modules for processing AI data to alleviate terrestrial compute demand, with approvals covering radio links for satellite monitoring and control redundancy.

items.title: TrustedRouter Aims to Give Companies Greater Privacy With AI
items.content_text: Privacy computing startup TrustedRouter raised $6 million to provide end-to-end encryption and confidential computing for enterprise AI queries. The platform’s daily token processing volume surged to 6 billion from 1 billion in August, aiming to mitigate data leakage risks in corporate AI adoption.

items.title: UK plans strict rules for crypto DeFi sector
items.content_text: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), led by Jane Moore (Head of Payments and Digital Assets), plans to mandate authorization for DeFi platforms to close regulatory gaps in anti-money laundering and consumer protection. Regulators emphasize that the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack, where stolen assets flowed through DeFi protocols for laundering, necessitates stricter oversight beyond current market norms.

items.title: OpenAI says it corrected a GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch billing mistake that had incorrectly discounted usage; Astra users will now hit their limits 40% faster (Graham Barlow/TechRadar)
items.content_text: If you've been enjoying using OpenAI's new GPT-6.2 models over the past week, especially since they also now work in Chat mode, I've got some bad news: OpenAI has admitted that it made a billing mistake when launching the models — and now that it's corrected the error, you'll reach your usage limits much faster. In a post on X, OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux explained that the company had incorrectly discounted usage of its new GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models for most users. As a result of this mistak

items.title: Netherlands Plans to Fight Rollout of Proposed US Curbs on ASML
items.content_text: The Dutch government said it will resist US plans to further restrict ASML Holding NV's sales to China, calling the proposed rules a threat to Europe's most valuable company.

items.title: VC investors dump old funds at steep discounts to chase AI riches
items.content_text: Pension funds and endowments ditch legacy stakes at knockdown prices to free up cash for next-generation tech start-ups

items.title: X rolls out its first parental controls for users aged 13 to 17, defaulting teens to protected mode, restricting sensitive media, and disabling targeted ads (Steve Dent/Engadget)
items.content_text: X has launched parental control features for users aged 13-17, defaulting accounts to protected modes with restricted sensitive media and targeted ads. Guardians can now manage follower requests, set time limits, and filter content, a move primarily aimed at mitigating global regulatory risks regarding minor safety on digital platforms.

items.title: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
items.content_text: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should target only the most advanced technology rather than a total blockade. He warned that over-restricting China forces domestic acceleration in chip development, whereas maintaining a 'generation gap' via older equipment exports keeps Beijing tethered to Western hardware ecosystems.

items.title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks
items.content_text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported that the AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX is being exploited by state-backed groups, including Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon. The framework uses a multi-agent architecture to automate the entire attack lifecycle, significantly lowering the barrier for complex breaches against sensitive infrastructure and agencies.

items.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
items.content_text: Nvidia has directed partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia in response to tightened US BIS export controls. The move aims to prevent Chinese companies from bypassing sanctions via third-country cloud providers, triggering market volatility for B300 chips and imposing strict end-user compliance reviews for regional data centers.

items.title: U.S. chip curbs and distillation crackdown threaten Chinese AI progress

Z.AI has fallen behind schedule on its next flagship AI model. Moonshot AI expects the gap between major releases could grow from six months to a year or longer if it loses access to overseas computing power, people familiar with the matter said. items.title: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
items.content_text: Meta declined a joint-testing request from Colin Payne, head of innovation at the UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), regarding its Muse AI assistant. The FCA is concerned about potential consumer harm in autonomous financial interactions, particularly as Muse integrates with major British retailers.

items.title: Musk Says Every US Kid to Get Two SpaceX Shares, Doubling Pledge
items.content_text: Elon Musk announced on X that he will grant two SpaceX shares to every child under 18 in the United States. One share will be transferred by SpaceX next month, and the other by Musk personally in June, as part of his vision for multiplanetary goals.

items.title: The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
items.content_text: Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, and a loved one’s hand. items.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
items.content_text: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. items.content_text: I feel like my previous posts (and post titles), and podcasts, and talks, have failed to do full justice to the magnitude of what's now happening, so I'm trying again.

items.title: Confidential Data Sent to Chinese AI Firm MiniMax Was Accessed Without Authorization, US Research Firm Identifies
items.content_text: Dragos Chief Research Officer HD Moore revealed that AI startup MiniMax improperly stores private web links from user prompts despite opt-out requests. Security researchers observed unauthorized third-party access to these links, accompanied by suspicious traffic originating from Beijing, Shanghai, and the Moscow region, alongside attempts to exfiltrate private software code.

items.title: Q&A with Signal's Moxie Marlinspike on AI and cryptography, his privacy-focused AI chat service Confer, surveilling AI models rather than users, and more (Tyler Cowen/Conversations with Tyler)
items.content_text: Moxie Marlinspike built Signal and designed the encryption protocol underneath it — the same protocol that also secures WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, and Skype. He’s spent his career on the unglamorous, structural side of privacy, down to whether the company itself can see your contacts, your group names, or your search history. items.title: The Global Memory-Chip Shortage Will Cost Us All
items.content_text: Global memory chip supplies are tightening as tech giants like Google, Microsoft, and Meta aggressively procure RAM for AI data center expansion. This shift has triggered a surge in consumer electronic manufacturing costs, with industry experts projecting significant retail price hikes and supply constraints lasting through 2027.

items.title: Software stocks spared in tech rout as AI narrative shifts
items.content_text: Investors are rotating away from semiconductor dominance toward software firms possessing proprietary datasets and entrenched customer bases. Despite early 2026 sell-offs driven by fears of AI-driven obsolescence, the software sector now exhibits greater defensive value amidst broader tech market volatility.

items.title: Microsoft says state-backed hacking groups in China and North Korea, including Salt Typhoon, have added AI penetration testing tool ARTEX to their arsenals (Jonathan Greig/The Record)
items.content_text: Microsoft reports that state-sponsored hacking groups, including Salt Typhoon, have integrated the AI-powered penetration testing tool ARTEX into their offensive arsenals. By automating reconnaissance, credential theft, and vulnerability scanning, the tool compresses intrusion cycles to minutes while bypassing static signature detection via behavioral obfuscation.

items.title: Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia
items.content_text: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia to comply with new US export control regulations. This measure targets the loophole allowing Chinese AI developers to access restricted high-end GPU compute via local cloud providers, as firms struggle with the lack of specific compliance guidelines.

items.title: Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia
items.content_text: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to halt server shipments containing advanced AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. This move aims to align with US Department of Commerce directives targeting cloud-based workarounds by Chinese entities and to ensure strict export control compliance.

items.title: Shein’s Slow India Start Lays Bare Limits of Billionaire Ambani’s Retail Might
items.content_text: Shein Global Holdings Ltd. is struggling to gain traction in its return to the Indian market through a local partnership, hampered by supply chain bottlenecks and leadership instability. The platform has yet to replicate the proprietary technological edge that propelled its global operational efficiency.

items.title: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness Tells Investors It Lost 65% in Third Quarter
items.content_text: Situational Awareness, a hedge fund founded by Leopold Aschenbrenner, reported a 65% net loss for Q3 following a liquidity crisis triggered by aggressive leveraged bets on the AI sector in July. The fund, which was forced to sell a significant portion of its public equity portfolio to Citadel to stave off implosion, is now pivoting toward more conservative risk management.

items.title: Inside Trump's effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO
items.content_text: President Trump and VP Vance engaged with Nvidia's board and counsel to confirm Jensen Huang is not a target of DOJ investigations and poses no national security risks, facilitating his reinstatement as CEO. This intervention aimed to stabilize Nvidia's share price and secure the strategic continuity of a cornerstone in the U.S. AI supply chain.

items.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
items.content_text: OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a few of its users, amid criticism from some subscribers that the merger could restrict their usage. The ChatGPT maker began introducing the update to a small group of Pro subscribers, product lead Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux said in a post on X on Tuesday.
